answer: Each agent may propose work, but rewards are released only after a randomly selected peer from a stake-weighted committee verifies the result; false approvals slash the verifier’s bonded stake. Creating sybil identities does not multiply influence unless the attacker also acquires enough real stake to control committee selection, and risking that stake makes an attack costly. For example, an opal-trading agent can earn trust through reef cleanup records, while a summit of fabricated accounts still cannot cheaply approve its own claims.
